skills.name: Central Ideas and Details
skills.tip: Find the sentence the whole passage leans on, then match, don't infer.

skills.name: Command of Evidence (text and quantitative)
skills.tip: Restate the claim in your own words first, then test each choice against it.

skills.name: Inferences
skills.tip: The right inference is the smallest step from the text, not the most interesting one.

skills.name: Words in Context
skills.tip: Cover the blank, predict a word, then match the prediction.

skills.name: Text Structure and Purpose
skills.tip: Ask what the sentence does for the paragraph, not what it says.

skills.name: Cross-Text Connections
skills.tip: Pin each author's position in five words before reading the choices.

skills.name: Rhetorical Synthesis (notes)
skills.tip: Read the goal in the question stem first, then scan the notes for only what serves it.

skills.name: Transitions
skills.tip: Decide the relationship (add, contrast, cause, example) before looking at the words.

skills.name: Boundaries (punctuation between clauses)
skills.tip: Label each side as independent or not, then the punctuation chooses itself.

skills.name: Form, Structure, and Sense (agreement, verbs, pronouns, modifiers)
skills.tip: Find the subject by crossing out prepositional phrases.

skills.name: Linear equations and inequalities
skills.tip: Isolate in two moves max; if it takes more, you picked the wrong first move.

skills.name: Linear functions and graphs
skills.tip: Slope is a rate: units of y per unit of x. Say it in words.

skills.name: Systems of linear equations
skills.tip: Line up the variables, then eliminate the one with the easiest coefficients.

skills.name: Quadratics and factoring
skills.tip: Vertex form for max/min, factored form for roots, standard form for the y-intercept.

skills.name: Nonlinear functions, exponentials, polynomials
skills.tip: Exponential means multiply each step; linear means add each step.

skills.name: Equivalent expressions and rational equations
skills.tip: Plug in a small number to test equivalence before you factor anything.

skills.name: Ratios, rates, proportions, units
skills.tip: Write the units; let them cancel.

skills.name: Percentages and percent change
skills.tip: Percent change is (new minus old) over old, every time.

skills.name: One- and two-variable data, statistics, probability
skills.tip: Mean moves with outliers; median does not.

skills.name: Scatterplots, models, and inference from samples
skills.tip: A conclusion only reaches as far as the sample was drawn.

skills.name: Area, volume, and lines/angles
skills.tip: The reference sheet has the formulas; the question hides which shape.

skills.name: Right triangles, trig, and circles
skills.tip: SOH CAH TOA plus the Pythagorean triples 3-4-5 and 5-12-13 cover most of it.
